root_cause.text: The `v9fs_apply_options()` function in the 9p filesystem applies parsed mount flags to `v9ses->flags` using a bitwise OR (`|=`) operation without first clearing the default access mode flags set by `v9fs_session_init()`, causing multiple conflicting access mode bits to be set simultaneously when a user specifies a custom access option.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check to clear the default access mask (`v9ses->flags &= ~V9FS_ACCESS_MASK`) before applying the user-specified flags (`v9ses->flags |= ctx->session_opts.flags`). The commit message explains that because of the `|=` operation, mounting with "access=user" leaves both the default `V9FS_ACCESS_CLIENT` and the user-specified bits set, which fails exact-value access mode checks.

intent_record.how: This prevents the default access flags from being combined with the new access flags, ensuring the correct access mode is set.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability. In `v9fs_session_init()`, `v9ses->flags` is initialized with default access flags (e.g., `v9ses->flags = V9FS_ACCESS_USER;` on line 433). Then, `v9fs_apply_options()` is called, which applies the parsed options using `v9ses->flags |= ctx->session_opts.flags;` on line 399. Because it uses a bitwise OR (`|=`) without clearing the default access mode flags first, any custom access option specified by the user (which is parsed into `ctx->session_opts.flags`) will be merged with the default flags, resulting in multiple conflicting access mode bits being set simultaneously.
